I need to verify memory_c2 (low-cost vendor switch) to confirm whether switching primary supply is genuinely low-risk and whether the savings would meet the 18% target, and memory_c6 (multi-year commitment with incumbent) to confirm whether a multi-year renewal can unlock enough volume pricing to absorb the mandated cut without adding delivery risk. If memory_c6 confirms that multi-year renewal meaningfully reduces unit cost while preserving service scope and integration stability (consistent with memory_c1's record of stable integration), then renew_incumbent achieves the cost reduction through volume pricing without the onboarding risk of a vendor switch, which is critical given the 14-day window and zero buffer. Switching primary vendors in 14 days with no buffer and a line already at 94% capacity carries unacceptable delivery risk even if unit cost is lower. The alternative actions (add_second_source, defer_decision) do not address the imminent contract expiry. Negotiate_terms is subsumed within a renewal and already evidenced by memory_c4. I will pull the archives to confirm before final commitment.
